```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
library(colorRamps)
```

```{r}

birdsurveys <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ccber-restoration/ncos-bird-surveys/refs/heads/main/data/aggregated/dryad_2017-2023/doi_10_5061_dryad_bvq83bkhz__v20240617/NCOS_Monthly_Bird_Surveys_2017-2023.csv")

summary(birdsurveys) # checking for data errors
# Count has 6 na's
# slough water elevation has 2703 na's
# all variables appear to have correct data type
# no extreme outliers for numeric data

```

```{r,warning = F}

# determining the number of observations per year
# all years have similar numbers of observations (mean ~ 1827) except for 2017, which only has ~400

yearrange <- unique(birdsurveys$Year)
obsperyear <- data.frame(year = yearrange,count = NA*7)

for(i in 1:7){obsperyear$count[i] <- length(which(birdsurveys$Year == yearrange[i]))}

obsperyearno2017 <- obsperyear %>% filter(count > 500)
mean(obsperyearno2017$count) # mean number of observations per year excluding 2017

# visualizing the distribution of bird count per year
# appears to be identical for every year?

birdsurveys$Year <- as.factor(birdsurveys$Year)

ggplot(data = birdsurveys,aes(x = Year,y = Count,fill = Year))+
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.9,outliers = F)+
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.1,color = "grey")+
  ylim(c(0,5))

```

```{r}

# determining number of survey dates per year
# does each individual observation date signify an individual survey, or are there sometimes multiple surveys per date?

length(unique(birdsurveys$Observation.Date)) # 885 total surveys across 2017-2023

# number of unique observation dates per year
# 2021 and 2022 have totals in the 100s, but the other 5 years have only a handful of unique observation dates - seems incorrect

#surveys_per_year <- data.frame(year = yearrange,count = NA*length(yearrange))
#for(i in 1:7){
#  tempdf <- birdsurveys %>% filter(Year == yearrange[i])
#  surveys_per_year$count[i] <- length(unique(tempdf$Observation.Date))
#}

# manual verification of information determined by previous data frame
# determined that high number of total unique observation dates is result of reporting time of day in addition to date

testdf <- birdsurveys %>% filter(Year == 2021)
unique(testdf$Observation.Date)

# removing time of day from observation date variable in new data frame
# correct determination of the number of observation dates, or unique surveys, per year

birdsurv_justdates <- birdsurveys
birdsurv_justdates$Observation.Date <- substr(birdsurv_justdates$Observation.Date,1,10)
surveys_per_year_correct <- data.frame(year = yearrange,count = NA*length(yearrange))
for(i in 1:7){
  tempdf <- birdsurv_justdates %>% filter(Year == yearrange[i])
  surveys_per_year_correct$count[i] <- length(unique(tempdf$Observation.Date))
}

```

```{r}

length(unique(birdsurveys$Species)) # 169 different species

length(unique(birdsurveys$General.Type)) # 13 different general types

# visualization of counts of the different general types
# terrestrial insectivores have highest count by far
# cormorants and kingfishers have lowest counts - most specific general type?
# hard to tell colors apart

ggplot(data = birdsurveys,aes(x = General.Type,fill = General.Type))+
  geom_bar(alpha = 0.9)+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.text.x = element_blank(),axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))+
  labs(y = "Count",fill = "General Type")

```

```{r,warning = F}

# analyzing terrestrial insects by substrate

tinsect <- birdsurveys %>% filter(General.Type == "Insectivores - Terrestrial")

#unique(tinsect$Substrate)
#which(tinsect$Substrate == "")

tinsect_substrate <- birdsurveys %>% filter(General.Type == "Insectivores - Terrestrial" &
                                              Substrate != "")

# pie chart of substrate type proportion
# four most common substrates, each <= 25%: bare ground and the three vegetation types

numsubs <- length(unique(tinsect_substrate$Substrate))
col <- primary.colors(numsubs) # primary colors easier to distinguish

ggplot(data = tinsect_substrate,aes(x = "",y = Count,fill = Substrate))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity")+
  coord_polar(theta = "y")+
  scale_fill_manual(values = col)+
  theme_void()

# per survey visualization of terrestrial insect observation count per top 5 most inhabited substrate

top5 <- c("Bare ground","Fence","Vegetation - Herbaceous","Vegetation - Shrub","Vegetation - Tree")

tinsect_substrate %>% filter(Substrate == top5 & Year != 2017) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Substrate,y = Count,size = Count,color = Substrate))+
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8)+
  facet_wrap(~ Year)+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.text.x = element_blank(),axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# visualization of terrestrial insect count per top 5 substrate distributions

tinsect_substrate %>% filter(Substrate == top5 & Year != 2017) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Substrate,y = Count,size = Count,fill = Substrate,color = Substrate))+
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.8)+
  facet_wrap(~ Year)+
  theme(axis.title.x = element_blank(),axis.text.x = element_blank(),axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# 2017 excluded because of lower total observations

```
